summary: The C recording reaches a trapped nonsteed mastodon at step 297 and farlook auto-description at step 298. pager.c:look_at_monster() describes a visible trapped monster only for BEAR_TRAP, pits (including SPIKED_PIT), or WEB; it obtains the text with trapname(tt, FALSE) and marks the trap seen. js/pager.js had the same already-wired function and imported trapname, but instead read an undeclared TRAP_DESCRIPTIONS table. The corrected function now follows the C predicate, trapname display behavior, and tseen update.

source.branch: In look_at_monster(), when mtrapped and cansee() hold, obtain t_at() and set tt to NO_TRAP when absent. For BEAR_TRAP, is_pit(tt), or WEB, append trapped-in text using an(trapname(tt, FALSE)) and set t->tseen.

evidence: The exact v73 admission evaluation reports ReferenceError `TRAP_DESCRIPTIONS is not defined` at segment 0 step 298, when getpos farlook describes the mastodon after the real bear-trap landing at step 297. The C screen says `mastodon, trapped in a bear trap`.

upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:look_at_monster() lines 422-555 obtains the trap type or NO_TRAP, tests BEAR_TRAP || is_pit(tt) || WEB, appends `trapname(tt, FALSE)`, and sets t->tseen. `is_pit()` includes PIT and SPIKED_PIT in include/rm.h.

The production caller path is getpos.c:getpos -> auto_describe -> do_screen_description -> look_at_monster. js/getpos.js:auto_describe() calls do_screen_description(); js/pager.js:look_at_monster() is used by do_screen_description and lookat. The function now uses the corresponding exported constants and existing trapname() implementation; no source callee is skipped.

After the correction, a fresh C/JavaScript differential of challenges/cases/v73/v73-nonsteed-bear-farlook-action2.recipe.session.json matches all 1,978 RNG calls and 373 screens/cursors. The focused test also verifies the trap description and tseen side effect through lookat().
